source_caption:
Tenet remains one of the most confusing films of all time  yet also one of Christopher Nolan’s most once-in-a-lifetime achievements. Very few filmmakers would even attempt something this structurally insane. That surreal moment when cars seem to move backwards, crashes look reversed, and time itself feels broken, this is Tenet’s inversion concept in action. In this sequence, objects and vehicles aren’t rewinding… they’re moving forward in reverse entropy, creating that impossible, mind-bending visual effect. It’s chaos, but with physics behind it. ~  Classic Nolan.

One of Tenet’s craziest production challenges: scenes involving inversion had to be designed twice once for forward motion and once for reversed playback so the physics and movement would still look believable. Many of the jaw-dropping highway stunts were filmed practically, with real vehicles and large-scale effects instead of relying purely on CGI which is exactly why the scene feels so disturbingly real. Nolan didn’t just film action… he engineered time.

source_details.synopsis: Tenet (stylized in all caps, previously as TENƎꓕ) is a 2020 science fiction action film written and directed by Christopher Nolan, who also produced it with his wife, Emma Thomas. It stars John David Washington, Robert Pattinson, Elizabeth Debicki, Dimple Kapadia, Michael Caine, and Kenneth Branagh. The film follows a CIA officer who is recruited into a secret organization, tasked with tracing the origin of objects that are traveling backward through time and their connection to an attack by the future. Nolan took over five years to write the screenplay after deliberating about Tenet's central ideas for more than a decade. Pre-production began in late 2018, casting took place in March 2019,
